The reporter's shader from issue #2202, compiled at -HV 2018 (the HLSL version dxc
defaulted to when this was filed in 2019; at today's default -HV 2021 the front end
rejects the vector-condition `?:` before codegen runs, so the bug is never reached).

What to look for, pane by pane:

  dxc_1_6_2112  and  dxc_trunk (plain)
      Both fail identically:
        error: DXIL intrinsic overload must be valid.
        note: at '... call double @dx.op.dot3.f64(i32 55, ...)'
      The bug is unchanged between CE's oldest DXC and trunk.

  dxc_trunk with -Vd  (validation disabled)
      This is the one that shows the actual defect rather than its symptom.
      The compile SUCCEEDS and emits:
        %10 = select i1 %7, double 1.500000e+02, double 1.000000e+02
        %13 = call double @dx.op.dot3.f64(i32 55, double %10, ...)
      DXIL's Dot3 op is declared with overloads "hf" -- half and float only
      (utils/hct/hctdb.py). There is no f64 Dot3, so the validator is correct
      to reject this module: -Vd does not work around the bug, it just ships
      DXIL no runtime will accept. The defect is that codegen produced it.

  fxc_10_0_19041 (/T ps_5_0)
      Contrast: FXC compiles the same source without complaint. It does not
      promote the literal-float ternary to double.

Root cause visible in the -Vd pane: `frac(p) < 0.5 ? 150.0 : 100.0` resolves to
double, so `dot` picks its double overload -- which HLSL has (gen_intrin_main.txt
declares dot over `numeric`) but DXIL cannot express.
